newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade active at $66-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade active at $66-feedlots.

text.p: Trade in Plains-area feedlot cattle was active on Tuesday as packers raised their bids by $2 per cwt to $66 to a price most feedlots found acceptable, livestock dealers said.
The sales mopped up most of the showlist in Texas which was estimated this week at around 102,000 to 103,000 head.
USDA reported confirmed sales in Texas/western Oklahoma of 63,600 head bringing the total for the week, including formulated and previously contracted supplies, to 97,500 head.
The bulk of trade last week was at $64 per cwt.
Strong beef prices contributed to the market's strength.
Light trade was anticipated on Wednesday, possibly again at $66, cattle feeders said.
"You could see a few trading at $66 tomorrow (Wednesday) but with beef higher again you are not going to see anybody taking less than $66," one Oklahoma source said.
USDA boxed beef cut-out values at midday Tuesday jumped $2.23 to $1.38 per cwt higher after posting similar gains on Monday.

Dealers noted there may be deliveries against August live cattle on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange if cash cattle prices do not rise further next week (or futures prices fall). The first day for delivery intentions is August 4.

August closed Tuesday at 67.650 cents a lb, a premium of 1.65 cents to the current cash price of $66 per cwt (66 cents a lb). Dealers said any premium above 1.50 cents would make it worthwhile delivering cattle.
"If we don't trade at $67 next week, then I think you will see some deliveries," one Oklahoma cattle feeder said.
